Yes, at 16 you can test a max, but it should be earned and done with care. A few ground rules:

Build a base first. A max test makes sense after several months of consistent training with solid technique on that lift, not as a way to start out.

Use a spotter, or safety pins in the rack, and warm up with a ramp of lighter sets. Stop the attempt if your form breaks down.

Don't do it often. Most lifters test a few times a year at most. Heavy sets of 3 to 5 reps will tell you nearly the same thing and build strength with less risk.

A lot of coaches skip true 1-rep maxes for teens altogether and track progress with rep maxes instead, like your best set of 5. That's a perfectly good way to go.

If you train with a school coach or a trainer, run the plan by them so someone's watching your technique. Which lift are you thinking of testing?
